passages.text: Then the LORD said to Moses on Mount Sinai, “Speak to the Israelites and say to them: When you enter the land that I am giving you, the land itself must observe a Sabbath to the LORD.
passages.sermon:
The LORD spoke to Moses.
The LORD was on Mount Sinai.
The LORD gave Moses a message.
The LORD told Moses to speak to the Israelites.
The LORD said, "You will enter the land I am giving you."
The LORD said, "The land must rest."
The LORD said, "The land must have a Sabbath for the LORD."
passages.original: וַיְדַבֵּ֤ר יְהוָה֙ אֶל־ מֹשֶׁ֔ה בְּהַ֥ר סִינַ֖י לֵאמֹֽר׃ דַּבֵּ֞ר אֶל־ בְּנֵ֤י יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ וְאָמַרְתָּ֣ אֲלֵהֶ֔ם כִּ֤י תָבֹ֙אוּ֙ אֶל־ הָאָ֔רֶץ אֲשֶׁ֥ר אֲנִ֖י נֹתֵ֣ן לָכֶ֑ם וְשָׁבְתָ֣ה הָאָ֔רֶץ שַׁבָּ֖ת לַיהוָֽה׃

passages.text: For six years you may sow your field and prune your vineyard and gather its crops.
passages.sermon:
God spoke to Moses on Mount Sinai.
God gave instructions to the Israelites.
God said, “You will enter the land I am giving you.”
For six years, you may plant seeds in your field.
For six years, you may trim your vineyard.
For six years, you may gather the crops from your land.
passages.original: שֵׁ֤שׁ שָׁנִים֙ תִּזְרַ֣ע שָׂדֶ֔ךָ וְשֵׁ֥שׁ שָׁנִ֖ים תִּזְמֹ֣ר כַּרְמֶ֑ךָ וְאָסַפְתָּ֖ אֶת־ תְּבוּאָתָֽהּ׃

passages.text: But in the seventh year there shall be a Sabbath of complete rest for the land—a Sabbath to the LORD. You are not to sow your field or prune your vineyard.
passages.sermon:
God spoke to Moses on Mount Sinai.
God gave instructions to the Israelites.
God said, “When you enter the land I give you, you must follow my commands.”
In the seventh year, the land must rest completely.
This rest is called a Sabbath for the LORD.
You must not sow your field in the seventh year.
You must not prune your vineyard in the seventh year.
passages.original: וּבַשָּׁנָ֣ה הַשְּׁבִיעִ֗ת שַׁבַּ֤ת שַׁבָּתוֹן֙ יִהְיֶ֣ה לָאָ֔רֶץ שַׁבָּ֖ת לַיהוָ֑ה שָֽׂדְךָ֙ לֹ֣א תִזְרָ֔ע וְכַרְמְךָ֖ לֹ֥א תִזְמֹֽר׃

passages.text: You are not to reap the aftergrowth of your harvest or gather the grapes of your untended vines. The land must have a year of complete rest.
passages.sermon:
God gave Israel a law for the land.
The land must rest every seventh year.
This year is called a Sabbath year.
You must not reap the aftergrowth of your harvest.
You must not gather the grapes from your untended vines.
The land must have a year of complete rest.
passages.original: אֵ֣ת סְפִ֤יחַ קְצִֽירְךָ֙ לֹ֣א תִקְצ֔וֹר וְאֶת־ עִנְּבֵ֥י נְזִירֶ֖ךָ לֹ֣א תִבְצֹ֑ר שְׁנַ֥ת שַׁבָּת֖וֹן יִהְיֶ֥ה לָאָֽרֶץ׃

passages.text: Whatever the land yields during the Sabbath year shall be food for you—for yourself, your manservant and maidservant, the hired hand or foreigner who stays with you, and for your livestock and the wild animals in your land. All its growth may serve as food.
passages.sermon:
God commanded a Sabbath year for the land.
During this year, the land must rest.
Whatever the land produces in the Sabbath year will be food.
You may eat from it.
Your male servant may eat from it.
Your female servant may eat from it.
Your hired worker may eat from it.
The foreigner living with you may eat from it.
Your livestock may eat from it.
The wild animals in your land may eat from it.
All the land’s produce will be for food.
passages.original: וְ֠הָיְתָה שַׁבַּ֨ת הָאָ֤רֶץ לָכֶם֙ לְאָכְלָ֔ה לְךָ֖ וּלְעַבְדְּךָ֣ וְלַאֲמָתֶ֑ךָ וְלִשְׂכִֽירְךָ֙ וּלְתוֹשָׁ֣בְךָ֔ הַגָּרִ֖ים עִמָּֽךְ׃ וְלִ֨בְהֶמְתְּךָ֔ וְלַֽחַיָּ֖ה אֲשֶׁ֣ר בְּאַרְצֶ֑ךָ תִּהְיֶ֥ה כָל־ תְּבוּאָתָ֖הּ לֶאֱכֹֽל׃ס

passages.text: And you shall count off seven Sabbaths of years—seven times seven years—so that the seven Sabbaths of years amount to forty-nine years.
passages.sermon:
God gave Israel a law about time and rest for the land.
God told the people to count years in a special way.
You must count seven periods of seven years.
Each period is seven years long.
You must do this seven times.
Seven times seven years equals forty-nine years.
You must count a total of forty-nine years.
passages.original: וְסָפַרְתָּ֣ לְךָ֗ שֶׁ֚בַע שַׁבְּתֹ֣ת שָׁנִ֔ים שֶׁ֥בַע שָׁנִ֖ים שֶׁ֣בַע פְּעָמִ֑ים וְהָי֣וּ לְךָ֗ יְמֵי֙ שֶׁ֚בַע שַׁבְּתֹ֣ת הַשָּׁנִ֔ים תֵּ֥שַׁע וְאַרְבָּעִ֖ים שָׁנָֽה׃

passages.text: Then you are to sound the horn far and wide on the tenth day of the seventh month, the Day of Atonement. You shall sound it throughout your land.
passages.sermon:
God gave Israel a command.
God told them to sound a horn.
They must do this on the tenth day of the seventh month.
This day is called the Day of Atonement.
They must sound the horn everywhere in their land.
passages.original: וְהַֽעֲבַרְתָּ֞ שׁוֹפַ֤ר תְּרוּעָה֙ בַּחֹ֣דֶשׁ הַשְּׁבִעִ֔י בֶּעָשׂ֖וֹר לַחֹ֑דֶשׁ בְּיוֹם֙ הַכִּפֻּרִ֔ים תַּעֲבִ֥ירוּ שׁוֹפָ֖ר בְּכָל־ אַרְצְכֶֽם׃

passages.text: So you are to consecrate the fiftieth year and proclaim liberty in the land for all its inhabitants. It shall be your Jubilee, when each of you is to return to his property and to his clan.
passages.sermon:
God gave Israel a command.
God told them to set apart the fiftieth year.
They must make this year holy.
They must announce freedom in the land.
This freedom is for every person living there.
This fiftieth year is called the Jubilee.
During the Jubilee, each person must return to his own land.
Each person must also return to his own family.
passages.original: וְקִדַּשְׁתֶּ֗ם אֵ֣ת שְׁנַ֤ת הַחֲמִשִּׁים֙ שָׁנָ֔ה וּקְרָאתֶ֥ם דְּר֛וֹר בָּאָ֖רֶץ לְכָל־ יֹשְׁבֶ֑יהָ יוֹבֵ֥ל הִוא֙ תִּהְיֶ֣ה לָכֶ֔ם וְשַׁבְתֶּ֗ם אִ֚ישׁ אֶל־ אֲחֻזָּת֔וֹ וְאִ֥ישׁ אֶל־ מִשְׁפַּחְתּ֖וֹ תָּשֻֽׁבוּ׃

passages.text: The fiftieth year will be a Jubilee for you; you are not to sow the land or reap its aftergrowth or harvest the untended vines.
passages.sermon:
The fiftieth year is called the Jubilee.
This year will be special for you.
You must not plant seeds in your land during this year.
You must not gather the crops that grow by themselves.
You must not pick grapes from vines that you did not tend.
passages.original: יוֹבֵ֣ל הִ֗וא שְׁנַ֛ת הַחֲמִשִּׁ֥ים שָׁנָ֖ה תִּהְיֶ֣ה לָכֶ֑ם לֹ֣א תִזְרָ֔עוּ וְלֹ֤א תִקְצְרוּ֙ אֶת־ סְפִיחֶ֔יהָ וְלֹ֥א תִבְצְר֖וּ אֶת־ נְזִרֶֽיהָ׃

passages.text: For it is a Jubilee; it shall be holy to you. You may eat only the crops taken directly from the field.
passages.sermon:
The fiftieth year is called the Jubilee.
The Jubilee year is holy for you.
You must treat this year as special and set apart.
You may eat crops from the field during the Jubilee.
You may only eat what grows naturally in the field.
You must not plant new seeds or harvest as usual during the Jubilee.
passages.original: כִּ֚י יוֹבֵ֣ל הִ֔וא קֹ֖דֶשׁ תִּהְיֶ֣ה לָכֶ֑ם מִן־ הַ֨שָּׂדֶ֔ה תֹּאכְל֖וּ אֶת־ תְּבוּאָתָֽהּ׃

passages.text: In this Year of Jubilee, each of you shall return to his own property.
passages.sermon:
God commanded the Israelites to observe the Year of Jubilee.
The Year of Jubilee is the fiftieth year.
In the Year of Jubilee, each person must return to his own property.
Each person must go back to the land that belonged to his family.
passages.original: בִּשְׁנַ֥ת הַיּוֹבֵ֖ל הַזֹּ֑את תָּשֻׁ֕בוּ אִ֖ישׁ אֶל־ אֲחֻזָּתֽוֹ׃

passages.text: If you make a sale to your neighbor or a purchase from him, you must not take advantage of each other.
passages.sermon:
God gave this command to the Israelites.
God told them how to treat each other in business.
If you sell something to your neighbor, do not cheat him.
If you buy something from your neighbor, do not cheat him.
You must not take advantage of each other.
passages.original: וְכִֽי־ תִמְכְּר֤וּ מִמְכָּר֙ לַעֲמִיתֶ֔ךָ א֥וֹ קָנֹ֖ה מִיַּ֣ד עֲמִיתֶ֑ךָ אַל־ תּוֹנ֖וּ אִ֥ישׁ אֶת־ אָחִֽיו׃

passages.text: You are to buy from your neighbor according to the number of years since the last Jubilee; he is to sell to you according to the number of harvest years remaining.
passages.sermon:
God gave Israel the law of the Jubilee year.
The Jubilee year happens every fifty years.
In the Jubilee year, people return to their own land.
If you buy land from your neighbor, count the years since the last Jubilee.
Buy the land based on the number of years since the last Jubilee.
Your neighbor will sell to you based on the number of harvest years left until the next Jubilee.
The price depends on how many harvests remain before the next Jubilee.
passages.original: בְּמִסְפַּ֤ר שָׁנִים֙ אַחַ֣ר הַיּוֹבֵ֔ל תִּקְנֶ֖ה מֵאֵ֣ת עֲמִיתֶ֑ךָ בְּמִסְפַּ֥ר שְׁנֵֽי־ תְבוּאֹ֖ת יִמְכָּר־ לָֽךְ׃

passages.text: You shall increase the price in proportion to a greater number of years, or decrease it in proportion to a lesser number of years; for he is selling you a given number of harvests.
passages.sermon:
God gave laws to Israel about buying and selling land.
God told the people to be fair with each other.
If you buy land from your neighbor, count the years until the next Jubilee.
If there are many years left, you must pay a higher price.
If there are few years left, you must pay a lower price.
The price depends on the number of harvests you will receive.
Your neighbor is selling you only the harvests until the Jubilee.
passages.original: לְפִ֣י׀ רֹ֣ב הַשָּׁנִ֗ים תַּרְבֶּה֙ מִקְנָת֔וֹ וּלְפִי֙ מְעֹ֣ט הַשָּׁנִ֔ים תַּמְעִ֖יט מִקְנָת֑וֹ כִּ֚י מִסְפַּ֣ר תְּבוּאֹ֔ת ה֥וּא מֹכֵ֖ר לָֽךְ׃

passages.text: Do not take advantage of each other, but fear your God; for I am the LORD your God.
passages.sermon:
God speaks to the people of Israel.
God commands each person.
Do not take advantage of your neighbor.
Respect and fear your God.
I am the LORD your God.
passages.original: וְלֹ֤א תוֹנוּ֙ אִ֣ישׁ אֶת־ עֲמִית֔וֹ וְיָרֵ֖אתָ מֵֽאֱלֹהֶ֑יךָ כִּ֛י אֲנִ֥י יְהֹוָ֖ה אֱלֹהֵיכֶֽם׃

passages.text: You are to keep My statutes and carefully observe My judgments, so that you may dwell securely in the land.
passages.sermon:
God gave statutes and judgments to Israel.
God commands you to keep His statutes.
God commands you to carefully observe His judgments.
If you obey God's statutes and judgments, you will live securely in the land.
passages.original: וַעֲשִׂיתֶם֙ אֶת־ חֻקֹּתַ֔י וְאֶת־ מִשְׁפָּטַ֥י תִּשְׁמְר֖וּ וַעֲשִׂיתֶ֣ם אֹתָ֑ם וִֽישַׁבְתֶּ֥ם עַל־ הָאָ֖רֶץ לָבֶֽטַח׃

passages.text: Then the land will yield its fruit, so that you can eat your fill and dwell in safety in the land.
passages.sermon:
God is the LORD your God.
God gives commands and statutes to His people.
God promises to bless the land.
The land will produce its fruit.
You will eat until you are satisfied.
You will live safely in the land.
passages.original: וְנָתְנָ֤ה הָאָ֙רֶץ֙ פִּרְיָ֔הּ וַאֲכַלְתֶּ֖ם לָשֹׂ֑בַע וִֽישַׁבְתֶּ֥ם לָבֶ֖טַח עָלֶֽיהָ׃

passages.text: Now you may wonder, ‘What will we eat in the seventh year if we do not sow or gather our produce?’
passages.sermon:
God gave Israel laws for the land.
God commanded Israel to keep His statutes and judgments.
God promised Israel they would live securely in the land if they obeyed.
God told Israel to let the land rest every seventh year.
Israel might ask a question.
Israel might say, "What will we eat in the seventh year?"
Israel might worry because they do not sow in the seventh year.
Israel might worry because they do not gather their crops in the seventh year.
passages.original: וְכִ֣י תֹאמְר֔וּ מַה־ נֹּאכַ֤֖ל בַּשָּׁנָ֣ה הַשְּׁבִיעִ֑ת הֵ֚ן לֹ֣א נִזְרָ֔ע וְלֹ֥א נֶאֱסֹ֖ף אֶת־ תְּבוּאָתֵֽנוּ׃

passages.text: But I will send My blessing upon you in the sixth year, so that the land will yield a crop sufficient for three years.
passages.sermon:
God owns the land.
God speaks to the people of Israel.
God promises to act in the sixth year.
God will command His blessing for the people in the sixth year.
The land will produce enough crops in the sixth year.
The harvest from the sixth year will last for three years.
passages.original: וְצִוִּ֤יתִי אֶת־ בִּרְכָתִי֙ לָכֶ֔ם בַּשָּׁנָ֖ה הַשִּׁשִּׁ֑ית וְעָשָׂת֙ אֶת־ הַתְּבוּאָ֔ה לִשְׁלֹ֖שׁ הַשָּׁנִֽים׃

passages.text: While you are sowing in the eighth year, you will be eating from the previous harvest, until the ninth year’s harvest comes in.
passages.sermon:
God commanded Israel to let the land rest every seventh year.
In the eighth year, you will plant your fields.
You will eat from the old harvest during the eighth year.
You will continue eating from the old harvest until the harvest of the ninth year comes in.
passages.original: וּזְרַעְתֶּ֗ם אֵ֚ת הַשָּׁנָ֣ה הַשְּׁמִינִ֔ת וַאֲכַלְתֶּ֖ם מִן־ הַתְּבוּאָ֣ה יָשָׁ֑ן עַ֣ד׀ הַשָּׁנָ֣ה הַתְּשִׁיעִ֗ת עַד־ בּוֹא֙ תְּב֣וּאָתָ֔הּ תֹּאכְל֖וּ יָשָֽׁן׃

passages.text: The land must not be sold permanently, because it is Mine, and you are but foreigners and residents with Me.
passages.sermon:
God owns the land.
You must not sell the land forever.
You live on the land as foreigners with God.
You live on the land as residents with God.
passages.original: וְהָאָ֗רֶץ לֹ֤א תִמָּכֵר֙ לִצְמִתֻ֔ת כִּי־ לִ֖י הָאָ֑רֶץ כִּֽי־ גֵרִ֧ים וְתוֹשָׁבִ֛ים אַתֶּ֖ם עִמָּדִֽי׃

passages.text: Thus for every piece of property you possess, you must provide for the redemption of the land.
passages.sermon:
God owns the land.
You live on the land as foreigners and residents with God.
You may possess property in the land.
For every property you possess, you must allow the land to be redeemed.
passages.original: וּבְכֹ֖ל אֶ֣רֶץ אֲחֻזַּתְכֶ֑ם גְּאֻלָּ֖ה תִּתְּנ֥וּ לָאָֽרֶץ׃ס

passages.text: If your brother becomes impoverished and sells some of his property, his nearest of kin may come and redeem what his brother has sold.
passages.sermon:
God owns the land.
God gives the land to His people.
God commands His people to treat each other with care.
If your brother becomes poor, he may need to sell his property.
Your brother is a fellow Israelite.
If this happens, his closest relative may help him.
The nearest family member may buy back what was sold.
The relative redeems the property for his brother.
passages.original: כִּֽי־ יָמ֣וּךְ אָחִ֔יךָ וּמָכַ֖ר מֵאֲחֻזָּת֑וֹ וּבָ֤א גֹֽאֲלוֹ֙ הַקָּרֹ֣ב אֵלָ֔יו וְגָאַ֕ל אֵ֖ת מִמְכַּ֥ר אָחִֽיו׃

passages.text: Or if a man has no one to redeem it for him, but he prospers and acquires enough to redeem his land, he shall calculate the years since its sale, repay the balance to the man to whom he sold it, and return to his property.
passages.sermon:
A man may own land in Israel.
Sometimes, he may become poor.
He may sell his land.
He may have no relative to redeem the land for him.
Later, he may become prosperous.
He may earn enough money to buy back his land.
He must count the years since he sold the land.
He must calculate the value for those years.
He must pay the remaining amount to the man who bought the land.
Then, he may return to his property.
passages.original: וְאִ֕ישׁ כִּ֛י לֹ֥א יִֽהְיֶה־ לּ֖וֹ גֹּאֵ֑ל וְהִשִּׂ֣יגָה יָד֔וֹ וּמָצָ֖א כְּדֵ֥י גְאֻלָּתֽוֹ׃ וְחִשַּׁב֙ אֶת־ שְׁנֵ֣י מִמְכָּר֔וֹ וְהֵשִׁיב֙ אֶת־ הָ֣עֹדֵ֔ף לָאִ֖ישׁ אֲשֶׁ֣ר מָֽכַר־ ל֑וֹ וְשָׁ֖ב לַאֲחֻזָּתֽוֹ׃

passages.text: But if he cannot obtain enough to repay him, what he sold will remain in possession of the buyer until the Year of Jubilee. In the Jubilee, however, it is to be released, so that he may return to his property.
passages.sermon:
If a man sells his property because he is poor, but he cannot get enough money to buy it back, the property stays with the buyer.
The buyer keeps the property until the Year of Jubilee.
In the Year of Jubilee, the property is released.
The original owner returns to his property.
passages.original: וְאִ֨ם לֹֽא־ מָֽצְאָ֜ה יָד֗וֹ דֵּי֮ הָשִׁ֣יב לוֹ֒ וְהָיָ֣ה מִמְכָּר֗וֹ בְּיַד֙ הַקֹּנֶ֣ה אֹת֔וֹ עַ֖ד שְׁנַ֣ת הַיּוֹבֵ֑ל וְיָצָא֙ בַּיֹּבֵ֔ל וְשָׁ֖ב לַאֲחֻזָּתֽוֹ׃

passages.text: If a man sells a house in a walled city, he retains his right of redemption until a full year after its sale; during that year it may be redeemed.
passages.sermon:
A man may own a house in a city with walls.
If this man sells his house, he does not lose all rights to it immediately.
He keeps the right to buy back his house.
This right lasts for one full year after the sale.
During that year, he may redeem, or buy back, his house.
passages.original: וְאִ֗ישׁ כִּֽי־ יִמְכֹּ֤ר בֵּית־ מוֹשַׁב֙ עִ֣יר חוֹמָ֔ה וְהָיְתָה֙ גְּאֻלָּת֔וֹ עַד־ תֹּ֖ם שְׁנַ֣ת מִמְכָּר֑וֹ יָמִ֖ים תִּהְיֶ֥ה גְאֻלָּתֽוֹ׃

passages.text: If it is not redeemed by the end of a full year, then the house in the walled city is permanently transferred to its buyer and his descendants. It is not to be released in the Jubilee.
passages.sermon:
A man sells a house in a walled city.
The man has one year to redeem the house.
If the man does not redeem the house within one year, the house becomes the permanent property of the buyer.
The buyer keeps the house for himself and for his descendants.
The house does not return to the original owner in the Year of Jubilee.
passages.original: וְאִ֣ם לֹֽא־ יִגָּאֵ֗ל עַד־ מְלֹ֣את לוֹ֮ שָׁנָ֣ה תְמִימָה֒ וְ֠קָם הַבַּ֨יִת אֲשֶׁר־ בָּעִ֜יר אֲשֶׁר־ לֹא חֹמָ֗ה לַצְּמִיתֻ֛ת לַקֹּנֶ֥ה אֹת֖וֹ לְדֹרֹתָ֑יו לֹ֥א יֵצֵ֖א בַּיֹּבֵֽל׃

passages.text: But houses in villages with no walls around them are to be considered as open fields. They may be redeemed, and they shall be released in the Jubilee.
passages.sermon:
Houses in villages have no walls around them.
These houses are like open fields.
People may redeem these houses.
These houses will be released in the Jubilee.
passages.original: וּבָתֵּ֣י הַחֲצֵרִ֗ים אֲשֶׁ֨ר אֵין־ לָהֶ֤ם חֹמָה֙ סָבִ֔יב עַל־ שְׂדֵ֥ה הָאָ֖רֶץ יֵחָשֵׁ֑ב גְּאֻלָּה֙ תִּהְיֶה־ לּ֔וֹ וּבַיֹּבֵ֖ל יֵצֵֽא׃

passages.text: As for the cities of the Levites, the Levites always have the right to redeem their houses in the cities they possess.
passages.sermon:
The Levites are a special group among the Israelites.
The Levites live in certain cities.
The Levites own houses in these cities.
The Levites always have the right to redeem their houses.
This right to redeem never ends for the Levites.
passages.original: וְעָרֵי֙ הַלְוִיִּ֔ם בָּתֵּ֖י עָרֵ֣י אֲחֻזָּתָ֑ם גְּאֻלַּ֥ת עוֹלָ֖ם תִּהְיֶ֥ה לַלְוִיִּֽם׃

passages.text: So whatever belongs to the Levites may be redeemed—a house sold in a city they possess—and must be released in the Jubilee, because the houses in the cities of the Levites are their possession among the Israelites.
passages.sermon:
The Levites are a tribe in Israel.
The Levites own houses in certain cities.
If someone redeems a house from the Levites, that house can be bought back.
If a house in a Levite city is sold, it must be released in the Jubilee year.
The houses in the cities of the Levites are their property among the Israelites.
The Levites have the right to reclaim their houses.
The Jubilee year restores these houses to the Levites.
passages.original: וַאֲשֶׁ֤ר יִגְאַל֙ מִן־ הַלְוִיִּ֔ם וְיָצָ֧א מִמְכַּר־ בַּ֛יִת וְעִ֥יר אֲחֻזָּת֖וֹ בַּיֹּבֵ֑ל כִּ֣י בָתֵּ֞י עָרֵ֣י הַלְוִיִּ֗ם הִ֚וא אֲחֻזָּתָ֔ם בְּת֖וֹךְ בְּנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

passages.text: But the open pastureland around their cities may not be sold, for this is their permanent possession.
passages.sermon:
The Levites are a tribe in Israel.
The Levites have cities.
Open pastureland surrounds these cities.
No one may sell this open pastureland.
This pastureland is the Levites’ permanent possession.
passages.original: וּֽשְׂדֵ֛ה מִגְרַ֥שׁ עָרֵיהֶ֖ם לֹ֣א יִמָּכֵ֑ר כִּֽי־ אֲחֻזַּ֥ת עוֹלָ֛ם ה֖וּא לָהֶֽם׃ס

passages.text: Now if your countryman becomes destitute and cannot support himself among you, then you are to help him as you would a foreigner or stranger, so that he can continue to live among you.
passages.sermon:
God gave this command to the Israelites.
Your fellow Israelite may become poor.
He may not be able to support himself while he is with you.
You must help him.
You must help him as you would help a foreigner or a stranger.
You must help him so that he can keep living with you.
passages.original: וְכִֽי־ יָמ֣וּךְ אָחִ֔יךָ וּמָ֥טָה יָד֖וֹ עִמָּ֑ךְ וְהֶֽחֱזַ֣קְתָּ בּ֔וֹ גֵּ֧ר וְתוֹשָׁ֛ב וָחַ֖י עִמָּֽךְ׃

passages.text: Do not take any interest or profit from him, but fear your God, that your countryman may live among you.
passages.sermon:
God gave this command to Israel.
God told Israel how to treat a fellow Israelite who became poor.
Do not take interest from your fellow Israelite.
Do not take profit from your fellow Israelite.
Fear God.
Let your fellow Israelite live with you.
passages.original: אַל־ תִּקַּ֤ח מֵֽאִתּוֹ֙ נֶ֣שֶׁךְ וְתַרְבִּ֔ית וְיָרֵ֖אתָ מֵֽאֱלֹהֶ֑יךָ וְחֵ֥י אָחִ֖יךָ עִמָּֽךְ׃

passages.text: You must not lend him your silver at interest or sell him your food for profit.
passages.sermon:
God speaks to the people of Israel.
God commands them to help a fellow Israelite who becomes poor.
Do not lend your silver to your poor brother and charge him interest.
Do not sell your food to your poor brother for profit.
passages.original: אֶ֨ת־ כַּסְפְּךָ֔ לֹֽא־ תִתֵּ֥ן ל֖וֹ בְּנֶ֑שֶׁךְ וּבְמַרְבִּ֖ית לֹא־ תִתֵּ֥ן אָכְלֶֽךָ׃

passages.text: I am the LORD your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt to give you the land of Canaan and to be your God.
passages.sermon:
The LORD is your God.
The LORD brought you out of the land of Egypt.
The LORD gave you the land of Canaan.
The LORD is your God.
passages.original: אֲנִ֗י יְהוָה֙ אֱלֹ֣הֵיכֶ֔ם אֲשֶׁר־ הוֹצֵ֥אתִי אֶתְכֶ֖ם מֵאֶ֣רֶץ מִצְרָ֑יִם לָתֵ֤ת לָכֶם֙ אֶת־ אֶ֣רֶץ כְּנַ֔עַן לִהְי֥וֹת לָכֶ֖ם לֵאלֹהִֽים׃ס

passages.text: If a countryman among you becomes destitute and sells himself to you, then you must not force him into slave labor.
passages.sermon:
If your fellow Israelite becomes poor and sells himself to you,
Do not make him work as a slave.
Treat him with dignity.
Do not force him into harsh labor.
passages.original: וְכִֽי־ יָמ֥וּךְ אָחִ֛יךָ עִמָּ֖ךְ וְנִמְכַּר־ לָ֑ךְ לֹא־ תַעֲבֹ֥ד בּ֖וֹ עֲבֹ֥דַת עָֽבֶד׃

passages.text: Let him stay with you as a hired worker or temporary resident; he is to work for you until the Year of Jubilee.
passages.sermon:
The man is your fellow Israelite.
He became poor.
He sold himself to you.
He must live with you.
He must be like a hired worker.
He must be like a temporary resident.
He will work for you.
He will do this until the Year of Jubilee.
passages.original: כְּשָׂכִ֥יר כְּתוֹשָׁ֖ב יִהְיֶ֣ה עִמָּ֑ךְ עַד־ שְׁנַ֥ת הַיֹּבֵ֖ל יַעֲבֹ֥ד עִמָּֽךְ׃

passages.text: Then he and his children are to be released, and he may return to his clan and to the property of his fathers.
passages.sermon:
An Israelite may become poor.
He may sell himself to you.
He is not your slave.
He works for you as a hired worker.
He works until the Year of Jubilee.
At the Year of Jubilee, you must release him.
He leaves you.
His children leave with him.
He returns to his family.
He returns to his ancestral property.
passages.original: וְיָצָא֙ מֵֽעִמָּ֔ךְ ה֖וּא וּבָנָ֣יו עִמּ֑וֹ וְשָׁב֙ אֶל־ מִשְׁפַּחְתּ֔וֹ וְאֶל־ אֲחֻזַּ֥ת אֲבֹתָ֖יו יָשֽׁוּב׃

passages.text: Because the Israelites are My servants, whom I brought out of the land of Egypt, they are not to be sold as slaves.
passages.sermon: The Israelites are my servants.\r\nI brought the Israelites out of the land of Egypt.\r\nYou must not sell the Israelites as slaves.
passages.original: כִּֽי־ עֲבָדַ֣י הֵ֔ם אֲשֶׁר־ הוֹצֵ֥אתִי אֹתָ֖ם מֵאֶ֣רֶץ מִצְרָ֑יִם לֹ֥א יִמָּכְר֖וּ מִמְכֶּ֥רֶת עָֽבֶד׃

passages.text: You are not to rule over them harshly, but you shall fear your God.
passages.sermon:
God gave this command to the Israelites.
The Israelites must not rule harshly over their fellow Israelites.
Each Israelite must treat his brother with kindness.
Each Israelite must fear God.
passages.original: לֹא־ תִרְדֶּ֥ה ב֖וֹ בְּפָ֑רֶךְ וְיָרֵ֖אתָ מֵאֱלֹהֶֽיךָ׃

passages.text: Your menservants and maidservants shall come from the nations around you, from whom you may purchase them.
passages.sermon:
The Israelites are God's chosen people.
God brought the Israelites out of Egypt.
Israelites must not be sold as slaves.
Israelites must not rule harshly over each other.
Israelites may have male and female slaves.
Israelites may purchase slaves from the nations around them.
These slaves may be men or women.
These slaves do not come from among the Israelites.
These slaves come from the surrounding nations.
passages.original: וְעַבְדְּךָ֥ וַאֲמָתְךָ֖ אֲשֶׁ֣ר יִהְיוּ־ לָ֑ךְ מֵאֵ֣ת הַגּוֹיִ֗ם אֲשֶׁר֙ סְבִיבֹ֣תֵיכֶ֔ם מֵהֶ֥ם תִּקְנ֖וּ עֶ֥בֶד וְאָמָֽה׃

passages.text: You may also purchase them from the foreigners residing among you or their clans living among you who are born in your land. These may become your property.
passages.sermon:
The Lord spoke to the Israelites.
He gave them laws about servants and property.
Foreigners lived among the Israelites.
Some foreigners had families and children born in the land of Israel.
The Israelites could buy servants from these foreigners.
They could also buy servants from the families of these foreigners.
These servants could become the property of the Israelites.
passages.original: וְ֠גַם מִבְּנֵ֨י הַתּוֹשָׁבִ֜ים הַגָּרִ֤ים עִמָּכֶם֙ מֵהֶ֣ם תִּקְנ֔וּ וּמִמִּשְׁפַּחְתָּם֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר עִמָּכֶ֔ם אֲשֶׁ֥ר הוֹלִ֖ידוּ בְּאַרְצְכֶ֑ם וְהָי֥וּ לָכֶ֖ם לַֽאֲחֻזָּֽה׃

passages.text: You may leave them to your sons after you to inherit as property; you can make them slaves for life. But as for your brothers, the Israelites, no man may rule harshly over his brother.
passages.sermon:
God gave laws to the Israelites.
God allowed Israelites to own slaves from foreign nations.
Israelites could give these slaves to their sons as an inheritance.
These slaves would become permanent property.
Israelites could make these slaves serve them for life.
Israelites could not treat fellow Israelites this way.
No Israelite could rule harshly over another Israelite.
passages.original: וְהִתְנַחֲלְתֶּ֨ם אֹתָ֜ם לִבְנֵיכֶ֤ם אַחֲרֵיכֶם֙ לָרֶ֣שֶׁת אֲחֻזָּ֔ה לְעֹלָ֖ם בָּהֶ֣ם תַּעֲבֹ֑דוּ וּבְאַ֨חֵיכֶ֤ם בְּנֵֽי־ יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ אִ֣ישׁ בְּאָחִ֔יו לֹא־ תִרְדֶּ֥ה ב֖וֹ בְּפָֽרֶךְ׃ס

passages.text: If a foreigner residing among you prospers, but your countryman dwelling near him becomes destitute and sells himself to the foreigner or to a member of his clan, he retains the right of redemption after he has sold himself. One of his brothers may redeem him: either his uncle or cousin or any close relative from his clan may redeem him. Or if he prospers, he may redeem himself.
passages.sermon:
A foreigner may live among you.
This foreigner may become wealthy.
Your fellow Israelite may live near this foreigner.
Your fellow Israelite may become poor.
He may sell himself to the foreigner who lives among you.
He may sell himself to a member of the foreigner’s family.
After he sells himself, he still has the right to be redeemed.
One of his brothers may redeem him.
His uncle may redeem him.
His cousin may redeem him.
Any close relative from his family may redeem him.
If he becomes able, he may redeem himself.
passages.original: וְכִ֣י תַשִּׂ֗יג יַ֣ד גֵּ֤ר וְתוֹשָׁב֙ עִמָּ֔ךְ וּמָ֥ךְ אָחִ֖יךָ עִמּ֑וֹ וְנִמְכַּ֗ר לְגֵ֤ר תּוֹשָׁב֙ עִמָּ֔ךְ א֥וֹ לְעֵ֖קֶר מִשְׁפַּ֥חַת גֵּֽר׃ אַחֲרֵ֣י נִמְכַּ֔ר גְּאֻלָּ֖ה תִּהְיֶה־ לּ֑וֹ אֶחָ֥ד מֵאֶחָ֖יו יִגְאָלֶֽנּוּ׃ אוֹ־ דֹד֞וֹ א֤וֹ בֶן־ דֹּדוֹ֙ יִגְאָלֶ֔נּוּ אֽוֹ־ מִשְּׁאֵ֧ר בְּשָׂר֛וֹ מִמִּשְׁפַּחְתּ֖וֹ יִגְאָלֶ֑נּוּ אֽוֹ־ הִשִּׂ֥יגָה יָד֖וֹ וְנִגְאָֽל׃

passages.text: He and his purchaser will then count the time from the year he sold himself up to the Year of Jubilee. The price of his sale will be determined by the number of years, based on the daily wages of a hired hand.
passages.sermon:
A man may become poor and sell himself as a servant to a foreigner living among the Israelites.
The man and his purchaser must count the years from the time he sold himself until the Year of Jubilee.
They must calculate the total number of years he will serve.
They must set the price of his sale according to the number of years.
They must use the daily wages of a hired worker as the standard for this calculation.
passages.original: וְחִשַּׁב֙ עִם־ קֹנֵ֔הוּ מִשְּׁנַת֙ הִמָּ֣כְרוֹ ל֔וֹ עַ֖ד שְׁנַ֣ת הַיֹּבֵ֑ל וְהָיָ֞ה כֶּ֤סֶף מִמְכָּרוֹ֙ בְּמִסְפַּ֣ר שָׁנִ֔ים כִּימֵ֥י שָׂכִ֖יר יִהְיֶ֥ה עִמּֽוֹ׃

passages.text: If many years remain, he must pay for his redemption in proportion to his purchase price.
passages.sermon:
A man may become poor and sell himself to a foreigner living among you.
If many years remain until the Year of Jubilee, he must pay for his redemption.
He must pay in proportion to his purchase price.
The payment depends on the number of years left.
passages.original: אִם־ ע֥וֹד רַבּ֖וֹת בַּשָּׁנִ֑ים לְפִיהֶן֙ יָשִׁ֣יב גְּאֻלָּת֔וֹ מִכֶּ֖סֶף מִקְנָתֽוֹ׃

passages.text: If only a few years remain until the Year of Jubilee, he is to calculate and pay his redemption according to his remaining years.
passages.sermon:
A man may sell himself as a servant to another.
The Year of Jubilee is a special year when all servants are set free.
If only a few years remain until the Year of Jubilee, the servant must count those years.
He must pay for his freedom based on the number of years left.
He pays only for the years that remain until the Jubilee.
passages.original: וְאִם־ מְעַ֞ט נִשְׁאַ֧ר בַּשָּׁנִ֛ים עַד־ שְׁנַ֥ת הַיֹּבֵ֖ל וְחִשַּׁב־ ל֑וֹ כְּפִ֣י שָׁנָ֔יו יָשִׁ֖יב אֶת־ גְּאֻלָּתֽוֹ׃

passages.text: He shall be treated like a man hired from year to year, but a foreign owner must not rule over him harshly in your sight.
passages.sermon:
The Israelite servant must be treated like a hired worker.
The owner must treat him as if he is hired year by year.
The foreign owner must not rule over the Israelite servant harshly.
You must not allow harsh treatment of the Israelite servant in your presence.
passages.original: כִּשְׂכִ֥יר שָׁנָ֛ה בְּשָׁנָ֖ה יִהְיֶ֣ה עִמּ֑וֹ לֹֽא־ יִרְדֶּ֥נּֽוּ בְּפֶ֖רֶךְ לְעֵינֶֽיךָ׃

passages.text: Even if he is not redeemed in any of these ways, he and his children shall be released in the Year of Jubilee.
passages.sermon:
The Israelite is a servant of the LORD.
He may become a servant to a foreign owner.
He may not be redeemed by his relatives or by paying his redemption in the ways described before.
If he is not redeemed in any of these ways, he will go free in the Year of Jubilee.
His children will go free with him in the Year of Jubilee.
passages.original: וְאִם־ לֹ֥א יִגָּאֵ֖ל בְּאֵ֑לֶּה וְיָצָא֙ בִּשְׁנַ֣ת הַיֹּבֵ֔ל ה֖וּא וּבָנָ֥יו עִמּֽוֹ׃

passages.text: For the Israelites are My servants. They are My servants, whom I brought out of the land of Egypt. I am the LORD your God.
passages.sermon:
The Israelites are My servants.
I am the LORD your God.
I brought the Israelites out of the land of Egypt.
The Israelites belong to Me as My servants.
passages.original: כִּֽי־ לִ֤י בְנֵֽי־ יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ עֲבָדִ֔ים עֲבָדַ֣י הֵ֔ם אֲשֶׁר־ הוֹצֵ֥אתִי אוֹתָ֖ם מֵאֶ֣רֶץ מִצְרָ֑יִם אֲנִ֖י יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֵיכֶֽם׃
